slots.label: Gas exchange in plants and fish

items.q: Which structure is the site of gas exchange in the lungs?
items.qAf: Watter struktuur is die plek van gasuitruiling in die longe?
items.explain: Alveoli have a large surface area and thin walls, so gases diffuse quickly.
items.explainAf: Longblasies het ’n groot oppervlak en dun wande, sodat gasse vinnig diffundeer.

items.q: Which feature increases the efficiency of gas exchange in alveoli?
items.qAf: Watter kenmerk verhoog die doeltreffendheid van gasuitruiling in longblasies?
items.explain: A large surface area and a rich capillary network speed up diffusion.
items.explainAf: ’n Groot oppervlak en ’n ryk kapillêrnetwerk versnel diffusie.

items.q: Why must alveolar surfaces be moist?
options: Gases must dissolve before they can diffuse
optionsAf: Gasse moet oplos voordat hulle kan diffundeer
items.explain: Gases diffuse through a thin film of water, so the surface must be moist.
items.explainAf: Gasse diffundeer deur ’n dun waterlaag, dus moet die oppervlak klam wees.

items.q: Gas exchange in fish takes place in the:
items.qAf: Gasuitruiling by vis vind plaas in die:
items.explain: Gills have many thin lamellae in contact with water.
items.explainAf: Kieue het baie dun lamelle in kontak met water.

items.q: In gills, blood flows opposite to the water. This is called:
items.qAf: In kieue vloei bloed teenoor die water. Dit word genoem:
items.explain: Countercurrent flow keeps a steep concentration gradient along the gill.
items.explainAf: Teenstroomvloei hou ’n steil konsentrasiegradiënt langs die kieu.

items.q: Which plant structures allow gas exchange through leaves?
items.qAf: Watter plantstrukture laat gasuitruiling deur blare toe?
items.explain: Stomata open to let CO₂ in and O₂ and water vapour out.
items.explainAf: Huidmondjies maak oop om CO₂ in te laat en O₂ en waterdamp uit.

items.q: The structures in fish through which gas exchange takes place.
items.qAf: Die strukture by visse waardeur gaswisseling plaasvind.

items.q: The tubes through which air enters the body of an insect.
items.qAf: Die buise waardeur lug die liggaam van ’n insek binnegaan.

items.q: The thin, moist surface over which gases are exchanged.
items.qAf: Die dun, klam oppervlak waaroor gasse uitgeruil word.

items.q: The breathing movement in which the diaphragm relaxes and air leaves the lungs.
items.qAf: Die asemhalingsbeweging waarin die diafragma ontspan en lug die longe verlaat.

items.text: During inhalation the [[]] intercostal muscles contract and the diaphragm [[]].
items.textAf: Tydens inaseming trek die [[]] interkostale spiere saam en die diafragma [[]].

items.q: Carbon dioxide is carried in the blood mainly as bicarbonate ions.
items.qAf: Koolstofdioksied word hoofsaaklik as bikarbonaat-ione in die bloed vervoer.
items.explain: True. Most CO₂ is carried in the plasma as hydrogen carbonate (bicarbonate) ions.
items.explainAf: Waar. Die meeste CO₂ word in die plasma as waterstofkarbonaat- (bikarbonaat-) ione vervoer.

items.q: The pressure inside the lungs increases during inhalation.
items.qAf: Die druk binne die longe neem tydens inaseming toe.
items.explain: False. The volume of the chest increases, so the pressure decreases and air rushes in.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Die volume van die borskas neem toe, dus neem die druk af en lug stroom in.

items.q: Give THREE ways in which alveoli are suited for gas exchange.
items.qAf: Gee DRIE maniere waarop alveoli geskik is vir gaswisseling.
points: There are millions of alveoli, giving a very large surface area.
Their walls are one cell thick (thin), so diffusion is quick.
They are moist and surrounded by many capillaries (a rich blood supply keeps the concentration gradient).
pointsAf: Daar is miljoene alveoli, wat ’n baie groot oppervlakte gee.
Hul wande is een sel dik (dun), dus is diffusie vinnig.
Hulle is klam en omring deur baie kapillêre (’n ryk bloedtoevoer handhaaf die konsentrasiegradiënt).
